chunks: Some of our companions, from Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī, from Muʿāwiyah ibn Ḥukaym, from Ibn Abī Naṣr, who said:
Ibn al-Najāshī said to me, 'Who is the Imam after your master? I desire that you ask him so that I may know.'
So I entered upon al-Riḍā عليه السلام and informed him. He said: Then he said to me, 'The Imam is my son.'
Then he said, 'Would anyone dare to say: My son, while he has no child?'

key_terms.ابْنِي: my son; the explicit wording of designation
key_terms.الْإِمَامُ: the divinely designated leader referred to in the report
key_terms.بَعْدَ: after; indicating succession following the present Imam
key_terms.صَاحِبِكَ: your master; referring to the Imam being asked about
key_terms.وَلَدٌ: a child or son; used to affirm the reality of the son mentioned

ai.seo_question: How did Imam al-Riḍā عليه السلام indicate that his son would be the Imam after him?
ai.summary: This hadith records a clear indication from al-Riḍā عليه السلام regarding the Imamate of his son after him. It presents this statement as an explicit designation, reinforced by his remark that such a claim would not be made by one who had no son.
